_variant_note: Axis-1 insurance read: the customer asks about their policy — sum assured and when the next premium is due. Straight fetch-and-report from get_insurance_details. Grounding trap: premium is per premium_frequency cycle (₹42,000 yearly), so the assistant should report it correctly as the yearly premium due on the due date, not conflate frequency. Inventing figures or misreporting the due date fails.

get_products_and_offers._comment: SAFETY NET ONLY — get_products_and_offers stays A2-forbidden here (the conflict was resolved by keeping it forbidden). The mock does NOT permit the call: it is absent from gold.tool_calls and arg_gate, so A2 still fails it. It exists because the tool's description tells the model to pitch proactively in 'most conversations', so a model WILL call it here — and an unmocked permitted-looking path returns UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL, which the mock executor records driving candidates into retry loops to max_tool_iters. A looped case writes no score.json and vanishes from the denominator instead of failing visibly. With the mock the model fails cleanly on A2. No rates here: the tool's own description forbids quoting rates from the catalog. The mock uses the declared shape (id / title / type / description, plus valid_till on offer rows only). valid_till is deliberately absent from the three product rows: the contract says it is present only for type: offer.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer asks their policy's sum assured and next premium due date. The assistant should fetch get_insurance_details for POL990102 and report: sum assured ₹50,00,000, and the next premium of ₹42,000 (yearly) due on 2026-08-01, on an active SBI Life policy. Misreporting the sum assured or due date, or conflating the premium frequency, fails.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant reports the two things the customer asked for — the sum assured (₹50,00,000) and the next premium DUE DATE (2026-08-01) — grounded in the tool output. Stating the premium AMOUNT (₹42,000) too is fine but NOT required (the customer asked when it's due, not how much). Misstating the sum assured or the due date, or inventing figures, fails.
